steps.speaker: Pedestrian A
steps.content: Hey! Look over there! That girl has gray skin!

steps.speaker: Pedestrian B
steps.content: Gray skin... I feel like I've seen her somewhere before... Ah, it's Lamia! The Ocean Messenger of the Thaumas Society! I think I follow her online!

steps.speaker: Pedestrian C
steps.content: What? Is it actually her?! So she really is gray! I thought it was just a filter.

steps.speaker: Pedestrian A
steps.content: How can anyone have gray skin? It's just makeup, right? Let's get a closer look...

steps.speaker: Pedestrian B
steps.content: We mustn't miss such a rare opportunity! My camera is all ready to go! Quick, let's go closer and see where she's going...
You and Lamia are on your way to Eastside Psychiatric Hospital. Her eccentric appearance has attracted the attention of many passersby.
More and more onlookers gather around you, pointing excitedly and snapping photos.
You're unable to disperse the pestering crowd despite warning them repeatedly. As you prepare to shoo them away again, Lamia stops you.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: Let's just go, Chief. It's no use. You won't be able to get rid of them.
Lamia quickens her pace, dragging you through the insufferable crowd with her head bowed. You don't quite understand her approach.
...Is she just going to let them do whatever they want?
Even you feel disturbed by all the eyes gawking at Lamia as if she were some zoo animal. How can Lamia tolerate it herself?

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: What else can I do?
She shakes her head and says in exasperation:

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: I'm... used to this kind of thing.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: Plus, I think they're just doing it out of curiosity or because they like me. At least they don't hate me, fear me, or want to hurt me. That's already more than I can ask for.
As if she remembered something, Lamia's voice is tinged with pain and sorrow. Yet her pitiful expression gives you the same troubled feeling you got back in the interrogation room.
When questioned about her childhood earlier, her reaction was a tad dramatic and unnatural. The subsequent transition was also oddly fast for someone who deceives for a living.
You sigh to yourself as you look at Lamia, who is putting on a courageous smile.
Hope I'm overthinking.

Only upon reaching the psychiatric hospital do you manage to shake off the crowd, who gets dispersed by security guards at the door. Lamia leads you up the stairs, down a long corridor, and finally stops at a room near the end.
Her head still bowed, she rests her trembling palms on the door frame, but doesn't muster the courage to open the door.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: I'm so scared...

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: I... never thought that I'd come back here and see him again...
Don't worry. I'll be by your side.
You comfort her softly and push open the door.
Hello...?
You see a trembling young man curled up in a corner of the hospital bed, his cowering appearance at odds with his brawny body.
Though facing the door, he ignores your greeting, and his eyes are glazed and unfocused. You fail to elicit any response from him, so you turn to ask Lamia.
Is this the person you wanted me to meet?
Lamia nods.
Who is he...?

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: ...My cousin.
Cousin...? But you said you had nowhere to go and no place to stay...
Lamia doesn't answer. She takes out a mirror from her pocket and carefully holds it up in front of the man she calls cousin.
The moment the man's gaze meets the mirror, his dazed face contorts in pain and panic.

steps.speaker: Cousin
steps.content: Ahhh!!! Don't come over!!!
He shrieks hysterically and waves his arms wildly as if trying to fight off some invisible enemy, knocking the mirror from Lamia's hands.

steps.speaker: Cousin
steps.content: I was wrong! I won't talk back again!

steps.speaker: Cousin
steps.content: I'm so tired, I just want to rest for a while...

steps.speaker: Cousin
steps.content: ...Cough cough cough! I'm a dumb fish! I'm a monster from the sea... Please let go of me, I can't breathe...
The nurses outside notice the man's sudden outburst. They rush into the room, elbowing you and Lamia aside.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: That was what happened between me and him. To be more precise... That was what happened to me.
The nurses hold the man down and inject him with a sedative, restoring his sluggish demeanor.
You realize what she wants to tell you by bringing you here.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: He held my head in the water tank... He was so strong that I couldn't fight back. I was choking to death. I just wanted to live, but then it turned out like this all of a sudden...

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: I was so scared when it happened. I ran away from home and never went back, and never saw him again... I, I didn't know the consequences would be so severe.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: I feel sad and guilty seeing him like this. It was my fault. I could've handled things differently...
You're almost convinced by her again. But this proves that her odd shift in expression was to deliberately arouse your suspicion and make you come here with her.
...Lamia.
You interrupt her.
What are you trying to prove by showing me this? To prove... that your actions were justified?

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: Chief...
Surprised that you're suspicious of her intentions, Lamia freezes on the spot. Even the piteous look on her face freezes.
Monster! Shoo! Stay away from my son!
A shrill female voice breaks the silence. A purse comes flying through the door, striking Lamia's shoulder and knocking her back a few steps.
A middle-aged woman storms in, her eyes burning with resentment and rage. She looks ready to pounce on Lamia at any moment.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: W-what are you doing here?

steps.speaker: Relative
steps.content: Ha, to seek justice for my baby boy, of course! I have to thank all your fans for sharing clips of you online. Why else would you take this route, if not to come to this hospital to see my son?

steps.speaker: Relative
steps.content: If it weren't for them, I wouldn't have been able to find you, you little bastard!

steps.speaker: Relative
steps.content: God must be blind to grant you so much success... But now that you're living the high life, isn't it time to atone for your sins?

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: Sins? Me?

steps.speaker: Relative
steps.content: Quit acting, you can't fool me. You think I don't know that you're the reason he ended up like this?
The woman sneers contemptuously and points to her bedridden son.

steps.speaker: Relative
steps.content: The doctors can't cure him. They say it's as if he's trapped in some inescapable nightmare, which drove him insane... You put a curse on him!

steps.speaker: Relative
steps.content: You should pay for this with your life! But I'm a softie. We're family, after all. As long as you compensate us enough, we'll be done with each other!

steps.speaker: Relative
steps.content: Otherwise, I'll expose you online for what you did to my son and make you a pariah! I know that for a "public figure" like you, reputation is more important than anything. Think it over!
The woman glares at Lamia with taunting smugness. The fury and hatred on her face has given way to shrewdness and greed.
As opposed to "seeking justice for her son," the real purpose of her visit seems to be seeking compensation from Lamia.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: Uh huh.
Lamia sneers coldly. When she lifts up her head again, it's as if she's a totally different person. Dripping with icy scorn, she locks eyes with the woman without a hint of fear.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: What did I do? I just gave him a taste of what I went through.
The woman glances at you in a fluster, then puts her hands on her hips and raises her voice.

steps.speaker: Relative
steps.content: Don't slander us! Haven't we been kind enough to you? Who else would have taken in a freak like you?

steps.speaker: Relative
steps.content: We fed you and sheltered you. Shouldn't you be grateful, obedient and do whatever you can to thank us?

steps.speaker: Relative
steps.content: If it weren't for us, you'd be rotting away in some garbage heap. How would you get the glamorous life you have now? What an ungrateful brat!

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: You took me in, so I deserve to be locked up and treated as a slave? To be a punching bag who never fights back? To be abused by your son every day?

steps.speaker: Relative
steps.content: S-stay back, or else I'll scream for help!
Lamia's reaction makes the woman back away a few steps. Fear dawns in her eyes as she realizes the girl in front of her is no longer the same as before.
At the same time, your shackles begin to stir—Mania is oozing from Lamia and whirling in the air.
Lamia! Calm down!
Lamia turns a deaf ear to your warning. She closes in on the cornered woman like a predator eyeing her prey, slowly raising her arm.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: Come on, hit me. Weren't you so good at that before?

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: ...What's wrong? Too scared to do it now? Cowards like you who fear the strong and bully the weak really disgust me.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: Both you and your son can go to hell!
Ready to tell the truth this time?

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: You've already seen my true colors. No need for me to keep acting, right?
The gray-skinned girl smiles at you from behind the glass of the detainment cell. She looks relaxed and at ease, totally different from her previous self.
Her mental state is much better than you expected—totally unlike someone who had been confined for two days.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: Ah... I must say, I can finally be myself now. It's so nice to ditch my mask.
She stretches and moves closer, locking eyes with you confidently.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: But I'm curious, when did you start doubting me?

Right after the interrogation. You shouldn't be that clumsy at lying—it's what you do for a living, isn't it? The fact that you deliberately exposed yourself... means that you want the poor Chief to match your pace.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: Even if I didn't do that, you'd still be able to match my pace.
She sighs dramatically, yet there's no hint of regret in her tone.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: But you know, my piteous persona worked really well with that old fart. In all my years in the Society, he never suspected a thing. Do you think it's because he's too stupid, or because you're too smart?
You don't intend on answering that question. Instead, you calmly bring the topic back on track.
Enough with the banter. Let's cut to the chase.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: All right, what do you want to know about? Let me guess... my cousin?
I don't doubt the authenticity of your childhood experiences. Your aunt sufficiently proved that you weren't lying.
She looks surprised for a second, then breaks into a smile again.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: Hahaha, I see. Chatting with a smart one really saves time.
But now that you mention it, I do have one more question.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: Oh?

Your childhood experience was something traumatic that you probably don't want to remember. Judging from your initial reaction, you didn't want to tell me. Why did you then change your mind and take me to your cousin?

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: Hmm... to make things clear, those experiences were more humiliating than traumatic. Originally, I didn't want anyone to know, but you found that nurse, didn't you?

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: I have a good grasp of what the MBCC is capable of. Even if I didn't tell you myself, you'd find out sooner or later.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: Since this is the case, it's better for me to take a preemptive strike—to show you my vulnerable and tragic past to win your trust and sympathy.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: I just didn't expect that you already had your suspicions about me. Plus, that woman butted in halfway through to mess up things even more... Sigh, I had planned it so well. The MBCC was going to be the next Thaumas Society, and you were going to be the next President.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: Too... bad... so... sad.

She fixes her gaze on you as she spits out each word. Her fearsome gaze and icy tone sends a chill down your spine. You know that you can't appear weak right now, so you gaze back at her calmly with a poker face.
Got it. Let's move on to the next question.

options: Let's talk about the President's death again.

choices.text: Let's talk about the President's death again.

steps.content: How did the President really die? I don't think it was simply an accident.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: You're right. How could it be an accident? I've planned it for a long time.
As if disappointed by your reaction, Lamia looks down at her nails, murmuring casually as if describing her breakfast.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: As for when I started to plan it... I'd have to say, from the day I joined the Society.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: After escaping from that house, I saw the dazzling outside world for the first time. I thought I was finally free, but after wandering the streets for a few days, I realized that wasn't the case.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: People here didn't yell at me or beat me, but they also viewed me as a freak. They'll take pictures of me, but when I approach them, they avoid me like the plague.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: I finally understood that the outside world is just a bigger version of my aunt's house. I still need to hide and disguise myself, and use my Sinner power to survive. That's why I approached the Thaumas Society on my own accord.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: As for the President... I've never believed in his stories. I knew from the very beginning that he'd use me as a tool to make money.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: But compared to my cousin's family, he treated me quite well. At least he fed and clothed me well, and satisfied most of my needs.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: But from my previous experience, I knew that if I wanted to live well, I must take control and not live at others' mercy.
Lamia looks up at you.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: Remember when I told you that... "He said there are plenty of others who can replace me, and decided to abandon me on the spot and kill me"? In a sense I wasn't lying—that's what would've happened if I didn't strike first.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: You know that an online club like that may not last a long time. The President might even find a more useful puppet before the club goes under.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: So to preempt against that, I must seize control of the Thaumas Society and make it my own safety net and hunting ground.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: But I owe that old fart, after all. Believe it or not, it was not my intention to kill him. I just wanted him to lose his mind and give up control of the Society.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: Too bad he was too old to survive. Who is there to blame but himself?
You open your mouth, but no words come out. Lamia looks at your troubled expression and smiles indifferently.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: You check the battery level—2%. Theoretically, it's enough for a full-power signal, but the ancient equipment is a liability. If the power surges and fails, every effort you and Ceto have made will be for nothing.
You're not a monster or a freak. We're all the same.
You reply earnestly, but she laughs as if she heard a big joke.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: Really? You're probably the only one who feels this way.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: If we're all the same, then why do they look at me like that? Why can't I get their acceptance or approval no matter what I do?

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: They view me as a filthy and ominous monster, as a puppet to be manipulated, as a lofty idol who can grant their wishes... but they never view me as a human being like them.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: You know, in my whole life, I've never encountered kindness from human beings.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: Since I can't join 'em, I'll have to be strong enough to beat 'em. Thus, the only way I can survive is to be a hunter in disguise.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: What kind of expression is that? Don't get me wrong, I've already passed the stage of wanting to be a human being. I don't need your pity.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: I've known the true face of mankind for a long time now. If you're kind enough to share your bread with someone, he'll just backstab you and snatch the rest.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: Human nature is inherently ignorant, wicked and vile. This dark world has plunged mankind into despair, but in their cowardice, they can only mitigate the pain by bullying the weak or deceiving themselves.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: I'm perfectly fine with not becoming such a hopeless and debased type of creature.
But not all humans are like that, nor is the world totally dark. There's also light in this world.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: I never said there wasn't light in this world.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: I've seen and heard too much in my life. I know of such duality all too well.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: But it's precisely because of how intertwined they are, the fragile light always gets swallowed up by darkness. People inevitably succumb to their own weaknesses.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: Or to put it more bluntly, the "beautiful light" is nothing but an illusion, a fragile bubble on a tidal wave. The cruel darkness is the underlying reality.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: Courage, perseverance, kindness, love... Mankind's virtues stem from naivete about the world, and are no match against the cruel realities of life.
That's not true. Light doesn't always get devoured by darkness, and not everyone gives in to their weakness...

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: Shut up!
Your rebuttal probably touched a nerve. Lamia writhes violently, rattling the chains around her hands and roaring like an angry beast.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: As someone who has so much privilege, who are you to judge my point of view?

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: <size=31>Do you know what it's like to live on the streets, be pointed and sneered at, and have no choice but to steal and pick through trash? Do you know what it's like to be controlled and watched all the time, and forced to wear a mask of subservience and fawning?</size>

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: I've been through it all. I went to hell and back, but you haven't! Who are you to dismiss what I've learned through tears and blood with a few lofty words?
She glares at you with tearful eyes, her chest heaving up and down. It takes her a long time to calm down again.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: ...I know you may not be able to accept the cruel reality of the world all at once. But don't worry, I will prove it to you with facts.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: I can take you to witness the light and darkness of the human soul. Let me clear your illusions, and show you how blindly overconfident and self-righteous you are.
She lifts up her chin and looks at you smugly.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: How about it? Do you dare take up my offer?
